hypothesis: After a sensor stops, the covariance grows by the model, the track-lost tick is predictable exactly from a declared radius rule, a lost track is neither updated nor admitted (and a refused update has no side effects), and reacquisition is an explicit, refusable operation with an exact initial covariance.
input_data: seed 732026: one synthetic camera run (30 active ticks)
seed 732028: 4000 turning-truth draws; turn rate 0.2 rad/s from the last estimated state
mathematical_model: P(n) = F(n dt) P F(n dt)^T + Q(n dt); lost when sqrt(lambda_max(P_pos) chi2_2(0.99)) > 1 m. Two-point initialization p = z2, v = (z2 - z1)/dt has error covariance [[R, R/dt], [R/dt, 2R/dt^2 + q dt/3 I]], equal to J blockdiag(R, R, Q(dt)) J^T for the error map J. A coordinated turn at omega has linear transition T(t); with white acceleration through the turn, E[NEES] = tr(P_f^-1 (T P T^T + Q_turn(t))) + d^T P_f^-1 d with d = (T - F) x_hat.
numerical_result: lost at tick 41 (predicted 41); refused fuse left the state unchanged: True; two-point max |z| 2.39, mean NEES 4.011; under the turn the coasting track becomes inconsistent after 44 ticks (99% ellipse radius 4.59 m; simulated mean NEES 13.30), while the 1 m rule had already declared loss after 11 ticks.
observation_model: Camera positions until tick 30, then none; readings after loss are offered to fuse, reacquire and admit.

title: Add sensor-track-lost behavior.
uncertainty: The lost tick and refusals are exact; the two-point and turning-truth statements carry Monte Carlo error (Bonferroni and single z bounds); the turn expectation is exact given the declared turn rate and process noise (Gauss-Legendre quadrature of a smooth integrand).
unresolved_assumptions: Under the correct model a coasting track stays consistent (T069); the radius rule is a policy for model validity and data association, not a statistical necessity.
Reacquisition assumes the readings belong to the lost target (no association ambiguity).
The turning truth adds white acceleration through the turn dynamics; other manoeuvre noise models change the random part of the expectation.
